title: Exothermic vs Endothermic Reactions
guideExplore: Switch between exothermic and endothermic reactions and watch the beaker glow, thermometer, and energy arrows respond.
guideCombustion: Combustion releases energy fast — watch the beaker glow hot red-orange as the temperature climbs (exothermic).
guideMeltingIce: Melting ice absorbs heat from its surroundings — watch the beaker turn cool blue as the temperature drops (endothermic).
guidePhotosynthesis: Photosynthesis absorbs light energy to build sugars — an endothermic process that cools its surroundings.
conditionsHint: Sim speed changes how quickly the temperature responds to the reaction.
learnMore: Exothermic reactions release energy (often as heat) to their surroundings, so the temperature rises. Endothermic reactions absorb energy from their surroundings, so the temperature falls.
